items.question: Under what condition does the act of applying meditation follow upon worship of the circle in this prescribed sequence?
premises: Worship of the circle must precede the application of meditation.
The duration of meditation is set by the correlative limit indicated here.
The prescribed practice links worship to sustained meditative application.
items.inference: Meditative application is to be undertaken for as long as the prescribed limit holds after worshipping the circle.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one applies meditation for as long as the prescribed duration lasts.

items.question: What claim about the range of linguistic forms encountered requires both heard and unheard languages to fall within a varied set?
premises: Languages of varied forms are indeed present in this context.
Both heard and unheard forms are counted among them.
The two categories are joined without excluding either.
items.inference: The set of languages comprises varied forms that include both those already heard and those not yet heard.
items.plain_english: Languages of varied forms indeed arise, and both unheard and heard ones are included.

items.question: What claim about the locus of hearing requires that it occur by, to, and in the self without recourse to an external source?
premises: Hearing occurs by the self alone as an emphatic fact.
It is directed to the self and takes place in the self.
The same reflexive term is used across instrumental, dative, and locative relations.
items.inference: The sound is heard reflexively within the self, by the self and for the self alone.
items.plain_english: By the self alone, indeed, it is heard by the self, to the self, and in the self.

rows.grounds: bahuvrīhi compound of balin, palita, and nis-muc

items.question: What claim about identity requires a figure freed from wrinkles and grey hair to be designated as a second form of the god of love?
premises: The figure is freed from wrinkles and grey hair.
That figure is identified as the god of love.
It is further designated as the second of its kind.
items.inference: A wrinkle-and-grey-hair-freed form appears as the second kāmadeva in this context.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, Kāmadeva appears as the second.

rows.grounds: root sthā with ati, present middle

items.question: What claim about method requires that one destroy wind and the like by speech while remaining like a mute?
premises: Wind and what follows it are to be destroyed by speech.
The agent is to remain like a mute in that action.
The two directives apply to the same person.
items.inference: By speech alone, he should destroy wind and the like, standing as one who is like a mute.
items.plain_english: He should destroy wind and the like by speech; indeed, he stands like a mute.

items.question: What claim about rank requires the seventh circle to be designated as supreme and as that which brings about the paralysis of an army?
premises: The seventh circle is addressed to the goddess.
It is characterized as making for the paralysis of an army.
It is further designated as supreme.
items.inference: The seventh circle is the supreme circle that paralyzes an army.
items.plain_english: The seventh circle, O goddess, is supreme and brings about the paralysis of an army.

items.question: What claim about efficacy requires vision to arise from afar for one who is devoted to worship and meditation in that circle?
premises: Vision arises from afar.
This occurs in relation to that circle.
It occurs for one who is devoted to worship and meditation.
items.inference: For one devoted to worship and meditation in that circle, vision is obtained from afar.
items.plain_english: And indeed, for one devoted to worship and meditation in that circle, vision comes from afar.

items.question: What claim about the powers of this circle requires it to produce killing, uprooting, paralysis, delusion, and what follows from them?
premises: The circle produces killing and uprooting.
It also produces paralysis, delusion, and the like.
These powers are addressed to the fortunate and beloved one.
items.inference: This circle brings about killing, uprooting, paralysis, delusion, and similar effects.
items.plain_english: Killing, uprooting, paralysis, delusion, and the like, O fortunate and beloved one.

items.question: What claim about attainment requires success to follow only from knowing the sixty-fourfold method and not from any other way?
premises: The method of eight times eight is to be known.
One who knows it succeeds.
Success does not occur otherwise.
items.inference: Attainment is possible only by knowing the eight-times-eight method, not by any other means.
items.plain_english: Indeed, having known the method of eight times eight, one succeeds; not otherwise.

rows.grounds: past participle of vac with pra

items.question: What claim about authority requires a doubtless ascertainment to be declared by the speaker with devotion and reasoning?
premises: The ascertainment is declared by the speaker.
It is declared with devotion and reasoning.
It is declared as doubtless.
items.inference: What is declared here is a doubtless ascertainment given by the speaker through devotion and reasoning.
items.plain_english: This doubtless ascertainment has indeed been declared by me with devotion and reasoning.

items.question: What claim about placement requires the eighth chapter to be designated as that which emerged in Candradvīpa?
premises: A chapter is designated as the eighth.
It is said to have emerged in Candradvīpa.
The locative marks its place of emergence.
items.inference: The eighth chapter is the one that emerged in Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: In Candradvīpa emerged the eighth chapter.

items.question: What claim about instruction requires the speaker to tell the beloved the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs?
premises: The arrangement of the rows of yoginīs is a defined teaching.
The speaker undertakes to tell it.
It is told to the beloved.
items.inference: The speaker will declare to the beloved the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, O beloved, the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

rows.grounds: long compound sarva-bhūcarī-sarva-gocara-yoginī with genitive plural

items.question: What claim about scope requires the total field-group to belong to all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs together?
premises: There are yoginīs who move on earth and yoginīs who move in the sky.
All of these are included without exception.
A single field-group belongs to all of them.
items.inference: The complete field-group belongs to all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.
items.plain_english: The whole field-group belongs to all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: What claim about classification requires all innate, all family-born, and all door-guarding yoginīs to be counted within the same set?
premises: Some are innate to all classes.
Some are born of all families.
Some are guardians of all doors, and all three groups are included.
items.inference: All innate yoginīs, all family-born yoginīs, and all door-guardians belong to the set in question.
items.plain_english: All innate, all family-born, and all door-guardians.

rows.grounds: past participle of kāś with pra

items.question: What claim about transmission requires the supreme secret among secrets to be revealed to the recipient by means of devotion?
premises: Among secrets there is a supreme secret.
That supreme secret is revealed to you.
Its revelation takes place by devotion.
items.inference: Out of devotion, the supreme secret among secrets has been revealed to you.
items.plain_english: The supreme secret among secrets has been revealed to you by devotion.

items.question: What claim about desire requires the speaker to wish now to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas?
premises: The speaker has a present wish.
That wish is to hear.
The object of hearing is the worship of the siddhas, to be heard from the gurus.
items.inference: Now the speaker wishes to hear from the gurus concerning the worship of the siddhas.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

rows.grounds: root dā with pra, causative optative

items.question: What claim about transmission requires the arrangement of the two syllables to be given in the case of others?
premises: There is a prescribed arrangement of two syllables.
This arrangement is to be given.
It is to be given in the case of others.
items.inference: One should give the arrangement of the two syllables to others.
items.plain_english: One should give the arrangement of the two syllables to others.

items.question: What claim about uniqueness requires that no knowledge equal to this one will exist again in the future?
premises: There is knowledge associated with this teaching.
No knowledge equal to it exists now by comparison.
No knowledge equal to it will come into being again.
items.inference: No knowledge equal to this will arise again in the future.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this; there will be none again.

rows.grounds: root vac, future first person middle

items.question: What claim about instruction requires the speaker to declare the method of names for them and to command the beautiful-eyed one to hear?
premises: A method concerning the names of those beings is to be stated.
The speaker will declare it.
The recipient is commanded to hear it.
items.inference: The speaker will declare the method of their names; the beautiful-eyed one is to hear it.
items.plain_english: I shall speak the method of their names; hear it, O beautiful-eyed one.

items.question: What claim about designation requires beings called family-impellers to be named as caturyuga in this address to the independent lord of gods?
premises: They are addressed in relation to the independent lord of gods.
They are designated as family-impellers.
They are named by the term caturyuga.
items.inference: The family-impellers are designated by the name caturyuga, O independent lord of gods.
items.plain_english: Caturyuga, thus, O independent lord of gods, are the family-impellers.

items.question: What claim about measure requires this Kaula teaching to be designated as supremely arisen and as measuring ten crores?
premises: This is a Kaula teaching.
It is designated as supremely arisen.
Its measure is said to be ten crores.
items.inference: This Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, is of the measure of ten crores.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, is of the measure of ten crores.

items.question: What claim about agency requires the yoginī named by wish to extend up to Māyā by the supreme wish of the siddhas?
premises: There is a yoginī named Icchā.
She is related to the siddhas.
By supreme wish she extends up to the end of Māyā.
items.inference: The yoginī named Icchā, by the supreme wish of the siddhas, extends up to Māyā.
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by the supreme wish of the siddhas, extends up to Māyā.

items.question: What claim about transmission requires the teaching concerning the Mothers to have been told again by the sky-movers to the goddess and the beloved?
premises: A teaching concerning the Mothers exists.
It was told again.
The tellers are the sky-movers, addressed to the goddess and the beloved.
items.inference: Again, the sky-movers have told the teaching concerning the Mothers, O goddess and beloved one.
items.plain_english: Again, O goddess, O beloved one, the teaching concerning the Mothers has been told by the sky-movers.

items.question: What claim about transmission requires the teaching concerning the earth-moving good-eaters to have been told by an earth-mover to the beloved?
premises: There is a teaching concerning the earth-moving good-eaters.
It was told by an earth-mover.
It is addressed to the beloved.
items.inference: The teaching concerning the earth-moving good-eaters has been told by an earth-mover, O beloved one.
items.plain_english: The teaching concerning the earth-moving good-eaters has been told by an earth-mover, O beloved one.
